newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi sees six-month Albania mission.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi sees six-month Albania mission.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Tuesday that he expected an Italian-led force due to secure humanitarian relief to stay in Albania for up to six months.

"We envisage a total of six months as an insuperable time frame and within which the force should be withdrawn," he told the Senate (upper house) at the start of a debate on a mission which has caused political turmoil in Italy.
"We foresee in any case that (the force) should be withdrawn at the latest within a month of the elections," he said.

Albania, swept by lawless violence last month in the wake of failed savings schemes, is ruled by a government of national unity ahead of early general elections scheduled to take place by the end of June.
Prodi told the Senate, which was due to vote on the mission later on Tuesday, that "Operation Alba" (sunrise) would consist of 6,000 men and include 2,500 Italians.
He said it would start deploying early next week, although advance contingents of Italian and other troops were due to leave in the next few days to pave the way for the full mission.
Operation Alba has United Nations approval to stay in Albania for three months, subject to possible extension.
France is planning to contribute some 1,000 troops, Greece 700, Turkey 500, Romania 400 and Spain 300. Austria and Denmark say they are also considering participation.

Italy's Chamber of Deputies was due to vote on the Albania mission on Wednesday. Prodi's government, which lacks a majority in the lower house, may be compelled to back an opposition motion on the force since its hard-left ally has refused its support.
